title: ACA s. 14 — Failure or impossibility to act

content.overview: Section 14 provides for termination of an arbitrator's mandate where the arbitrator becomes de jure or de facto unable to perform the functions or fails to act without undue delay.
content.glance: Section 14 provides for termination of an arbitrator's mandate where the arbitrator becomes de jure or de facto unable to perform the functions or fails to act without undue delay.
content.study:
Module 1: Inability
The distinction concerns legal incapacity and practical inability to perform the mandate; the provision is not a general remedy for every disagreement.

Module 2: Undue delay
Failure to act without undue delay is a statutory ground and the factual record must connect the delay to performance of the mandate.

Module 3: Court mechanism
Where the statutory conditions are disputed, the Act supplies the court mechanism identified in section 14.
